welcome.title: CLLG — Guided Tour
welcome.body: CLLG turns scans of Greek and Latin scholarship into structured TEI XML in seven steps: import, document, mask, OCR, structure, review and export. Recognition runs locally with Kraken. The demo project is the start of the editio princeps of Galen's De propriis placitis (V. Boudon-Millot & A. Pietrobelli, Revue des Études Grecques 118, 2005), distributed by Persée under a CC BY-NC-ND licence. It is full of small challenges; nothing you do in the tour is saved.

home-new-project.title: Step 1 · Import your document
home-new-project.body: Click «New project» to load a PDF or DjVu, then choose the pages to import: a range such as «2-40», or quick filters like «Skip covers». Each page becomes an image in a project folder on your machine. In the demo, page 1 is the Persée cover: it is skipped for OCR but kept in the project, because it records where the document comes from and under which licence.

home-sources.title: Other sources
home-sources.body: You can also start from a folder of page images, or from ALTO XML files with their images (e.g. exported from eScriptorium). ALTO import keeps each line's geometry; if the ALTO carries LADaS zone types, paragraphs, quotes and headings are detected automatically.

document-type.title: Step 2 · Say what the document is
document-type.body: Pick the kind of document: a Greek scholarly edition (CLLG) or a Latin or general document typed with LADaS zones. It chooses the layout model that detects the zones of each page, and how margins are handled: CLLG merges the section numbers of the margins into the text as <ref>, LADaS keeps margin text as its own <note>. The demo is Galen's Greek: CLLG. You can change this later, here or on the OCR page.

document-zones.title: Which zones to keep
document-zones.body:
The layout model knows a list of zone types (9 for CLLG, 37 for LADaS). For each, choose «Annotate» (the text is kept and tagged, e.g.

, and the zone can be edited in Review), «Keep text» (plain lines, no tag) or «Drop» (left out of the transcription). By default, running titles, page numbers and noise are dropped. On page 2 of the demo, «172 V. BOUDON-MILLOT ET A. PIETROBELLI» is a running title: once detected, it is left out of the text even without a mask.

masker-canvas.title: Step 3 · Mask what shouldn't be read
masker-canvas.body: Draw white rectangles over everything that is not the main text: masked areas are whited out before Kraken reads the page. Page 2 of the demo has three: the running head («172  V. BOUDON-MILLOT ET A. PIETROBELLI»), the line numbers in the left margin (5, 10, 15…) and the footnotes. Challenge: page 3 prints its line numbers in the right margin — does it need a mask too?

masker-tools.title: Masking tools
masker-tools.body: Rectangle mask (D) draws, Pointer (S) selects, Delete removes. «Copy to all pages» repeats a layout across the book; hover a thumbnail and click ⊘ to skip a page (like the cover). «Generate masks from ALTO regions» builds masks from imported zones and «Export COCO» saves them as training data.

ocr-models.title: Step 4 · Choose the Kraken models
ocr-models.body: Kraken uses a segmentation model (finds the lines) and a recognition model (reads them); with «Detect regions», a layout model also finds the zones chosen at step 2. The built-in models (Ancient Greek, and the CLLG and LADaS layout models) are downloaded once, on the app's first launch; choose Custom to load your own. «CPU threads» sets how much of the computer OCR may use — saved for this computer.

ocr-run.title: Run OCR
ocr-run.body: Click «Run OCR» to recognize the queued pages one at a time; results are cached, so you can stop and resume at any time. Each line is anchored with <lb n="…"/> so the text stays linked to its place on the image. Below: Kraken's raw output for the start of page 2 — a lowercase ν in the title, a stray υ, a lost «(ἐν)» and a missing iota subscript.

ocr-steps.title: Run only some steps
ocr-steps.body: OCR has three steps: Zones (layout), Lines (segmentation) and Text (recognition). «Only some steps» reruns just the ones you tick on the selected pages — including pages already reviewed — and keeps everything else: the Zones step, for instance, adds or updates the zones without touching a corrected word. Review offers the same buttons for the current page, in its Re-OCR panel.

config-hierarchy.title: Step 5 · Define the document structure
config-hierarchy.body: Describe how the text is divided and numbered. This treatise is divided into sections 1, 2, 3…, so the demo has a single level, «section», with Arabic numbers. The hierarchy drives the TEI <div> structure; it is optional: without it the TEI is cited by page only. The Bibliography section fills the TEI header's sourceDesc (the demo already cites the article).

config-format.title: Reference patterns
config-format.body: Choose the numbering system of each level: Roman (I II III), Arabic (1 2 3), Greek (α β γ), or a custom regex. Options: missing_first (the first number is not printed), allow_gaps, and milestone (a marker inside the text, such as a page reference, rather than a division).

review-editor.title: Step 6 · Review and correct
review-editor.body: The scan is on the left, the transcription on the right; the button at the left of the page bar hides the scan. Edit directly and save with ⌘S (⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z undo and redo); change page with the arrows at the top right or Ctrl+↑ / Ctrl+↓. Below: the same lines as the OCR step, after review. Challenge: page 3 still hides two OCR slips — find «ομὲν» and «τῆν».

review-image.title: Line boxes and zones
review-image.body: «Show line boxes» outlines every line; click one to jump to it in the editor. «Zones» shows the zones of the page, detected (dashed) or drawn (solid); each is linked to its tag in the text, and putting the caret in the text selects its zone. To change a zone's type, click its label on the image or in the zone list, or press T: type to filter («head», «mzh»…), Enter to pick; P, Q, H and C pick Paragraph, Quote, Heading and Continued directly. «Draw Zone» (G, pointer over the image) draws new zones and moves or resizes them; Delete removes one. In the demo, page 3 opens with a Continued zone: section 2 carries on from page 2, and the export joins them. To fix a badly segmented line, select it, press R over the image and draw its new box; «Re-OCR line» reads that line again.

review-tag-ref.title: Tag the section numbers
review-tag-ref.body: Select a section number and press ⌘R to wrap it in <ref>; the tag dock at the bottom assigns its level (here, 1 = section). Each level-1 <ref> opens a new <div> at export. Also: ⌘M <note>, ⌘Q <quote>, ⌘I <cit>, ⌘B <bibl>.

review-tools.title: Checking tools and Greek typing
review-tools.body: «2nd read» runs Kraken again and underlines disagreements; «Line» shows the image of the current line above the caret; the magnifier (⌘F) searches the page; «Latin» flags Latin letters inside Greek. β (⌘K) is a betacode keyboard, diacritics first: «)a» gives ἀ, «:» the ano teleia ·, «?» the Greek question mark, and «<» «>» the Leiden brackets ⟨ ⟩ that this edition uses for supplied words (page 2: «περὶ ⟨ὧν⟩»).

export-generate.title: Step 7 · Export
export-generate.body:
«Generate» builds one TEI P5 file for the whole document: each section opens a
, zones become and

, and a Continued zone is merged into the paragraph it continues — across the — as in the real output below. Every file can be cited by page (a citeStructure on ), and by section when there is a hierarchy. Words split at the line end, like «διά-» / «νοιαν», are joined with . The Per-page tab exports plain text, LADaS-tagged text, ALTO or pre-TEI; you can also export a searchable PDF or share the project as a zip.

finale.title: You're ready!
finale.body: Import a PDF, a folder of images or ALTO files and start your own edition; the tour can be replayed from the home screen or the sidebar. Help improve the models: sharing your original data — page images with their corrected transcriptions (ALTO or per-page exports; the final TEI is not required) — with the CLLG developers helps train better segmentation and recognition. The demo pages come from Persée (doi:10.3406/reg.2005.4610) under CC BY-NC-ND.

document.title: Document
document.subtitle: What kind of document this is, and which zones of the page to keep in the transcription. You can come back and change this at any time.

typeDescription.cllg: A Greek scholarly edition. The section markers in the margins (Stephanus, Bekker, chapter numbers…) are merged into the text as <ref>, longer margin text as an inline <note>. Uses the CLLG layout model.
typeDescription.ladas: A Latin or general document typed with the LADaS zone vocabulary. Margin text is kept as its own <note>. Uses the LADaS layout model, which knows many more zone types.

document.zonesSubtitle: The zone types the layout model detects. For each one, choose what the transcription keeps.
document.noRegionModel: Zone detection is off: every line is transcribed as it is, without zones. Turn on «Detect regions» to choose zones.
document.setAll: Apply to every type of this group
document.policyNote: Applies to the next OCR runs. On pages already OCRed, run the Zones step (OCR page) to update their zones; it never removes text already transcribed.

actionHint.annotate: Keep the text and the zone: tagged in the text and editable in Review
actionHint.keep: Keep the text only, as plain lines: no tag, no zone
actionHint.drop: Leave this text out of the transcription (the line boxes are kept)

models.title: Downloading the Kraken models
models.intro: The built-in OCR models are not part of the application: they are downloaded once from the release on GitHub ({{size}} MB) and kept for the next launches. Importing and masking work in the meantime; OCR needs them.
